messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'kestrelhealth-prod' GPU utilization at 100% for >5m. Queue length rising, requests 503-ing for tenant 'kestrelhealth'. Pager: @maria (oncall) @paula-sre. Link: https://redwood/inci/6500004321

maria (oncall): acked. paging paula. I'm grabbing metrics and will post ETA for initial mitigation in 2m.

paula-sre: looking now — tailing the pool agent logs and scheduler. Confirming: all 8 GPUs in kestrelhealth-prod are pinned by Kestrel tenant jobs; backlog of synchronous generation requests spiking to 1.2k. Latency P95 trending 4.8s -> 18s. Some 503s from queue timeouts.

evans-eng: @paula-sre is this isolated to their pool or are other tenants affected?

paula-sre: isolated to their dedicated pool. Other pools normal. Cause looks like a sudden traffic spike from KestrelHealth (maybe batch resend). Evidence: request_id samples: [kest-req-2301, kest-req-2310] — heavy long-context calls resetting KV cache frequently.

raj-cs: customer reported "increased error rates" via support ticket 78921. KestrelHealth on their weekly ingest window right now; they warned of high throughput but didn't request burst. Customer impact: ~12% of requests failing, major UX impact for their integrated clinician UI.

maria (oncall): options: 1) enable emergency burst for kestrelhealth-prod (+2 GPUs) 2) evacuate low-priority background jobs from pool 3) route excess traffic to hosted-compatible fallback model (lower throughput / cheaper) 4) ask customer to throttle. Need quick decision — what's the risk/latency for enabling burst?

alex-runtime: enabling burst will spin up two N8 GPUs in us-west-2; expected readiness ~70s. Policy requires @sre lead approval for >1 GPU burst, but incident bot allows temporary override for P0 customer-impact. Bursting will relieve queueing but increases cost. Alternative: we can drain non-critical jobs from pool in ~30s.

paula-sre: I propose: immediate drain low-priority pods and enable 1 GPU burst now, escalate to +1 more if queue doesn't drop in 90s. I'll run drain + burst commands.

paula-sre: running: ```rictl pool drain --pool kestrelhealth-prod --label priority=low --grace 10s```

incident-bot: ACTION: drain request accepted. Task id: drain-6500004321-1

paula-sre: now enabling burst: ```rictl pool burst --pool kestrelhealth-prod --add-gpus 1 --reason "emergency mitigation - tenant queueing" --expires 15m```

incident-bot: ACTION: burst request queued. Approval bypass used by oncall for P0 incident. Provisioning started (provider: aws-us-west-2).

maria (oncall): posting note to customer channel: "We're aware of elevated errors and are taking emergency measures (draining low-priority jobs + temporary capacity). Will update in 10m."

raj-cs: customer acknowledges — thanks, they asked for ETA on full resolution.

paula-sre: provision succeeded, new GPU online. Observability: queue length dropping from 1.2k -> 320 in 40s. P95 latency down to 6s. Error rate down to ~3%.

katie-product: good. We should keep fallback route in case it spikes again; can we auto-failover some percent to hosted variant?

alex-runtime: we can enable dynamic routing rule to divert 25% of traffic for kestrelhealth to 'rwd-hosted-small' model for 10m. Doing that would reduce load and quality slightly. Need consent from product/customer?

maria (oncall): do it as a circuit-breaker: enable 25% diversion now, notify customer. If errors remain >5% after 10m, escalate to full +1 GPU and notify billing.

alex-runtime: applying routing change... ```routectl set-diversion --tenant kestrelhealth --percent 25 --to rwd-hosted-small --ttl 10m```

incident-bot: ACTION: routing change applied. id route-6500004321-1

paula-sre: monitoring: after diversion+burst, queue now 90, P95 3.1s, errors 1.2%. Good immediate stabilization.

raj-cs: passing update to KestrelHealth support lead: "We've applied a temporary GPU burst and routed 25% of traffic to a hosted fallback. Monitoring closely; ETA for full recovery depends on their ingest window ending or we add capacity for longer."

maria (oncall): decision log: emergency mitigation steps executed: drained low-priority pods, +1 GPU burst (15m), 25% diversion to hosted fallback. If we see repeat within 15m, escalate to +1 GPU permanent reserve and open billing approval.

paula-sre: handing off monitoring to night oncall @paula-sre -> next oncall at 6500004500. I'll remain available for 20m.

maria (oncall): closing pager for active escalation. Will update incident record with timeline and mitigation commands.

katie-product: follow-up: schedule post-incident sync with KestrelHealth to discuss autoscale policy and whether they want reserved burst capacity next month.

paula-sre: noted. Incident severity: P1 (customer-facing, mitigated).
